inputs.title: The Thing
inputs.logline: When Bo’s big tail betrays how hard it is to meet new friends, Keen and Aida help him discover that the very thing he wants to hide may be the first thing everyone loves.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

beats.adultRead: The comedy is the impossibility of controlling every tell; Keen’s cover is doomed because he is still a kid in a too-big plan.
beats.emotionalIntent: Build the laugh through anticipation, release it with the sneeze, then button it with Fuzzby’s sleepy authority.

beats.need: She needs to trust the quiet signal and make room for someone else’s fear without taking over.
beats.kidRead: A magic bowl shows a squirrel who keeps packing but does not go anywhere.
beats.adultRead: The repetition is instantly recognizable as a child trying to make a hard transition feel controllable.
beats.emotionalIntent: Quiet wonder with a small ache under it; the vision should feel intimate, not flashy.

beats.storyBeat: Inside the hollow tree, Bo answers his offscreen Mum but bargains with time and his conker, delaying the Learning Circle by making “a minute” stretch absurdly. The safe room is cosy, but it is also a trap of postponement.
beats.want: Bo wants to put off leaving while sounding like he still intends to go.
beats.need: He needs to be witnessed in the stuck place instead of left alone with the loop.
beats.kidRead: Bo keeps finding reasons not to go yet, and his conker is like his little helper.
beats.adultRead: The offscreen parent call captures the morning-transition ache: encouragement from another room cannot cross the threshold for him.
beats.emotionalIntent: Tender comic avoidance; keep it small, domestic and recognisable.

vision.premise: Bo is due at the Learning Circle for the first time, but every step toward the door makes his tail poof with worry. Keen’s playful curiosity and Aida’s quiet truth help him move toward the group one step at a time, until the tail he feared becomes his way in.
vision.dramaticQuestion: Can Bo go to the Learning Circle without having to hide the part of himself that gives him away?
vision.theme: Belonging begins when the thing you were trying to hide is gently witnessed and welcomed.
vision.externalJourney: Keen fails to steal honey, is redirected by Aida, visits Bo’s hollow tree, walks him through the woods, helps him arrive at the Learning Circle, and returns home to find Fuzzby attempting his own honey heist.
vision.internalJourney: Bo moves from delaying and controlling every detail to taking a visible step forward with his worry still present, then letting his tail become play instead of proof that something is wrong with him.
vision.relationshipChanges: Bo and Keen shift from strangers at a doorway to easy friends; Bo and Aida move from cautious distance to shared truth; Bo and the Learning Circle group move from imagined judgement to delighted acceptance. Fuzzby and Zenny provide the comic echo: being ridiculous and still belonging.
vision.emotionalCurve: Playful mischief opens the episode, then narrows into Bo’s held-at-the-door worry. The woods give relief through play, dip again at the log, soften through Aida’s honesty, glow into the walk forward, burst into group joy, and settle in a warm, lightly comic garden coda.
vision.comedyCurve: The comedy starts with stealth, snore bubbles, pollen and sneezes; turns into tail-poof escalation and Keen’s useless-tail demonstration; blooms into group delight at the Learning Circle; and ends with Fuzzby’s flower-disguise failure and Zenny’s tiny crack of amusement.
vision.setupPayoffMap: The untouched honeycomb and Fuzzby’s “never ever” return in the final garden heist. Bo’s conker and repeated packing plant his need for control. The tail’s first unwanted poof pays off as a chosen game in the woods and then as the Learning Circle’s delight. Aida’s vision of Bo unable to move pays off in Bo walking forward under pink and blue light. “Every single time” moves from Aida’s truth to Bo’s own action phrase.
vision.visualMotifs: Closed/open thresholds, paws holding objects too tightly, Bo’s tail expanding beyond his control, the forest path as a visible line between home and belonging, and the honeycomb as comic temptation that remains untouched.
vision.sonicMotifs: Crunching steps, snore-bubble pops, sneeze blasts, the shave-and-a-haircut knock, tail POOFs, Aida’s bowl tone, rose and aquamarine glow tones, group cheers, and Zenny’s bookend Ommmm.
vision.climax: Aida and Keen each offer their crystal truth, pink and blue light join on the forest path, and Bo takes one step, then another, toward the Learning Circle.
vision.resolution: At the Learning Circle, Bo’s tail poofs in front of everyone and is met with wonder, cheering and play; later, he draws with Keen while Aida watches his settled belonging from the edge of the clearing.
vision.intendedFinalFeeling: Warm, giggly relief: the child feels the fun of the fluffy tail, while the adult feels the ache of a child being welcomed without needing to edit himself.

orderedEvents.text: Golden morning light. Dew sparkles on wildflowers. A honeycomb sits on a small stump. KEEN tiptoes toward it. He lifts his knees high with every step.
CRUNCH. CRUNCH. CRUNCH.
Keen freezes each time. He spots the honeycomb. His eyes widen. He LICKS HIS LIPS. He reaches toward the honey. FUZZBY the bee is asleep on top of the honeycomb.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
A small snore bubble grows from his nose. Keen reaches closer to the honey. POP! The bubble bursts. Keen FREEZES.

orderedEvents.speaker: Fuzzby
orderedEvents.text: ZZZZZ …
Another bubble slowly grows. Keen inches closer to the honey.
POP! The second bubble bursts.

beats.storyBeat: Keen attempts an exaggerated stealth mission toward Fuzzby’s honeycomb, but every crunchy step and snore-bubble pop makes the world more awake than he wants it to be. The beat is about borrowed boldness meeting tiny physical resistance.
beats.want: Keen wants to get close enough to take honey without waking Fuzzby.
beats.need: He needs to learn that rushing toward what he wants is not the same as being ready or unseen.
beats.kidRead: Keen is being silly-sneaky and the sleeping bee might wake up any second.
beats.adultRead: A child’s confidence is charmingly exposed by his own body and the environment; he is not as invisible as he thinks.
beats.emotionalIntent: Light suspense and giggly anticipation, with the honeycomb as the forbidden prize.

treatments.name: The Bowl Becomes a Door
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience begins inside a hush: a safe, resonant morning quiet where Aida’s bowl tone feels like the clearing itself is listening. Bo’s packing-and-unpacking loop introduces gentle concern without explanation. Then Keen’s sneezes burst through that quiet as physical comedy, not interruption for its own sake. The final feeling is forward motion: the grown-up has seen the need, the sneezy child has been included, and the mission begins with warmth still ringing in the air.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: Aida governs the scene. We are with her receptive stillness first: she is not searching frantically, she is making enough quiet for need to reveal itself. The turn is not simply that Keen sneezes; it is that Aida’s private knowing becomes shared action. Her line “Someone needs a little help today.” lands as grounded recognition, and her later invitation to Keen shows her growth in miniature: help does not have to arrive perfectly composed.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary dramatic mechanism: containment failing gently. The bowl tone opens outward; Bo’s packed things refuse to stay settled; Keen’s sneeze cannot stay hidden; Aida’s private concern cannot remain private. Comic mechanism: silence replacing explanation, then sound invasion. The clearing is so quiet that Keen’s “AHHHHCHHOOOOO!!!” feels much too large to hide, and Aida’s calm “Bless you” makes the sneeze funnier by refusing to scold it.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Aida performs thought through economy: grounded posture, slow breath, an attentive stillness that becomes slightly more purposeful when the vision clarifies. She does not “act concerned” broadly; concern shows in the length of her look and the careful placement of her words. Keen is first a bodily consequence before he is a participant: the sneezes expose where he has been and what he cannot control. When Aida calls him, his eagerness should outrun his recovery, so “Coming, Aida!” is sincere and a little defeated by the next sneeze.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene is built on circles becoming paths. The bowl’s vibration, the rose-lit vision, and Bo’s repetitive packing loop all feel circular and contained. After the sneeze breaks the quiet, the composition language opens into directional travel: Aida turns the circle of listening into a route toward Bo. The rose vision should fill the frame when it appears, with haze at the margins dissolving the clearing away; it must not read as a small object being inspected from a safe distance.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera is invited into Aida’s listening rather than stationed outside it. It may discover the vision as if drawn by the bowl tone, then be expelled back into morning clarity by the off-camera sneeze. It does not automatically hunt for Keen immediately; the first allegiance remains Aida’s reaction. Once she chooses to include him, the camera’s relationship changes from contemplative witness to gentle companion moving into action.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Aida’s stillness is the scene’s anchor, but it must not become dead staging. Her stillness has pressure inside it: tiny shifts of attention, hands settling, a breath held a fraction too long as Bo’s loop repeats. Bo’s vision supplies small repetitive motion. Keen supplies uncontrolled release. The contrast should be legible before any dialogue explains it: held tone, repeated rustle, explosive sneeze.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: The clearing begins as a resonant chamber, with morning dew and wildflowers present but softened by the bowl’s authority. During the vision, depth becomes emotional rather than geographic: Bo’s hollow-tree space feels close and sealed, with repeated packing motions pressing against the edges. When the sneeze lands, depth snaps back to the real clearing, making the environment feel awake again. Rose warmth remains as a trace; it does not become a triumphant blaze.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Begin with a sustained, unhurried ring. Let Bo’s packing loop repeat just long enough for the audience to understand stuckness without being told. Aida’s line is the quiet naming of purpose. Then the sneeze lands as a comic rupture. The rhythm should not become frantic after that; Aida absorbs the chaos and folds it into forward motion. The final sneeze is a button, not a derailment.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts are motivated only by changed knowing or changed state: entering the rose vision, being snapped out by the sneeze, and converting Aida’s attention into an invitation. Avoid routine reaction coverage. Hold Aida while the sneeze invades if her stillness is the joke; cut only when the audience needs new information or when the comic punctuation benefits from discovering Keen’s exposed state.
treatments.openingImage: A circular bowl holding a single visible vibration in golden morning, with Aida’s steady presence making the clearing feel quiet enough to hear a feeling before anyone explains it.
treatments.closingImage: Aida’s invitation has turned the listening circle into a path: rose warmth still faint in the clearing as Keen, still sneezy, is folded into her forward motion toward Bo.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not make this a safe elder-at-bowl tableau followed by a standard cutaway to the sneezer. The bowl tone must actively reshape the frame, and the sneeze must have enough spatial force to rupture that shape. If the camera merely observes Aida from a respectful distance, we lose the scene’s engine: private listening becoming shared going.

treatments.name: The Clearing Tries Not to Laugh
treatments.audienceExperience: This version lets children feel the suspense of a quiet place that is about to be ruined by a very loud body. The audience enjoys the serenity but is also waiting for it to break. Bo’s vision gives the scene its heart, then Keen’s sneezes give permission to laugh. The adult reward is Aida’s response: she does not protect the sacred calm from the messy child; she lets the messy child belong inside the next step.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The emotional point of view belongs to the clearing as held by Aida. Aida has made a space where small signals matter: a tone, a rustle, a repeated movement inside a vision. Keen’s arrival is experienced as the world failing to stay composed. The turn is Aida’s refusal to treat that failure as failure. Her calm transforms Keen from disturbance into helper.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary comic mechanism: environmental participation. The quiet clearing amplifies everything Keen is trying not to be. His sneeze is not just a sound; it shakes the mood of the place. Secondary mechanism: status change. Keen enters as the obvious culprit of the honeycomb aftermath, then Aida’s “Keen? Come with me” quietly promotes him into the mission. The joke and the invitation occupy the same breath.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Aida’s performance is warm containment: she lets the sneeze pass through the scene without flinching into annoyance. Her “Bless you” should feel automatic and kind, but her “Sounds like someone has been sniffing around Fuzzby’s honeycomb” carries a small knowing smile in the timing, not a lecture. Keen’s vocal performance should be huge, involuntary, and then instantly eager; he wants to answer the call properly, but his body keeps adding punctuation.
treatments.visualGrammar: The visual grammar contrasts sacred quiet with comic overexposure. Before the sneeze, the frame privileges negative space, soft morning air, and the bowl’s gentle resonance. The rose vision enters as a protected pocket of concern. After the sneeze, compositions become slightly less tidy: not chaotic coverage, but the clearing’s serenity has been physically dented. The world’s stillness becomes the straight face to Keen’s noise.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera begins as a quiet participant in the clearing, almost holding its breath with Aida. It is allowed to be surprised by the off-camera sneeze rather than politely waiting where Keen will appear. After the first sneeze, the camera may search by consequence: drifting toward disturbed flowers, pollen in the air, or Aida’s knowing attention before fully committing to Keen. The camera’s allegiance remains emotional clarity, not immediate identification of the noise source.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Stillness is the straight man. Aida, the bowl, and the clearing hold themselves with care; Keen’s sneeze punches through that restraint. Bo’s loop sits between them: small, repetitive, unable to progress. The scene escalates by enlarging what cannot be contained: first the vision’s concern, then Keen’s sneeze, then Aida’s invitation expanding the helper circle.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Use the clearing as a listening field. Space should feel open enough that the sneeze travels, but intimate enough that it is embarrassing. The rose-lit vision compresses around Bo’s loop, creating a private chamber inside the larger clearing. When Keen’s sneezes arrive, foreground elements can register the disturbance before the character is found, making the environment part of the gag without inventing new story business.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: The rhythm is hush, recognition, rupture, recovery, recruitment, button. Aida’s bowl tone and Bo’s repeated packing establish a gentle pulse. The first sneeze should feel too big for the established tempo. Aida restores rhythm with “Bless you,” then pivots into the honeycomb clue and the invitation. Keen’s final sneeze lands as the scene’s comic release after the emotional business has already moved forward.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Do not cut merely because someone speaks. Let the sound of the sneeze motivate the break in visual calm. Use cuts as comic punctuation and as changes in the scene’s social contract: private vision to public interruption, culprit to helper, calm to movement. Avoid action/consequence/reaction mechanics; the joke can live in Aida staying composed while the world around her admits Keen’s mess.
treatments.openingImage: A morning clearing arranged around quiet: the bowl’s held tone, Aida’s centred attention, and enough still air that even a tiny rustle would matter.
treatments.closingImage: Keen’s final “AHHHHCHHOOOOO!!!” hangs as comic punctuation while Aida’s path toward Bo has already begun, making the sneeze part of the team’s forward energy instead of an embarrassment left behind.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Resist polishing the clearing into unbreakable prettiness. The comedy requires a visible difference between the composed space before the sneeze and the slightly disturbed space after it. If every frame remains equally tidy, Keen’s body has not truly entered the scene.

treatments.name: The Vision Pulls Them Forward
treatments.audienceExperience: The audience is first drawn into a small mystery: who needs help, and why does the packing never become leaving? Bo’s loop creates a child-readable worry without using worry-words. Keen’s sneezes then rescue the scene from solemnity, and Aida’s kindness turns the laugh into momentum. The audience exits curious about Bo and delighted that the helper coming along is the least subtle bear in the clearing.
treatments.emotionalPointOfView: The emotional point of view is the need revealed by the vision, with Aida as the one sensitive enough to receive it. The scene does not belong to Aida’s authority alone or Keen’s comic arrival alone; it belongs to the pull of Bo’s stuckness. Aida’s strength is that she lets the pull redirect her. Keen’s value is that, once exposed, he becomes available to that same pull.
treatments.comicOrDramaticMechanism: Primary dramatic mechanism: concealment to revelation. Bo’s feeling is not named; it is revealed through the repeated packing and unpacking. Keen’s mischief is also not confessed; it is revealed through sneezes and Aida’s honeycomb clue. Comic mechanism: hiding failure. Keen tries to answer as if ready to join, but his body keeps revealing the honeycomb aftermath.
treatments.characterPerformanceStrategy: Aida should behave like someone receiving a signal, not someone commanding magic. Her attention narrows in the vision, then widens after the sneeze to include Keen. She never overplays discovery; the line “Someone needs a little help today” is quiet certainty. Bo’s vision performance is all action: packing, unpacking, returning to the same point. Keen’s performance is contrast: full-body eagerness interrupted by involuntary sneezes, with no self-pity and no need to explain himself.
treatments.visualGrammar: The scene is shaped by attraction. The bowl tone draws us inward; the vision draws us toward Bo’s loop; the sneeze yanks us outward; Aida’s invitation redirects both Aida and Keen toward the unseen next place. Instead of circle-to-path as the dominant pattern, this version uses pull-and-release: each visual state exerts force on the camera and characters, then the sneeze or invitation releases that force into a new direction.
treatments.cameraCharacterRelationship: The camera behaves like it can be summoned. It is pulled into the rose haze by Aida’s tone, held by Bo’s repeated action, then jolted free by Keen’s sneeze. It does not owe any character permanent position or symmetrical treatment. If the camera loses the clearing briefly inside the vision, that is desirable: Bo’s need should momentarily become the whole world. When Aida calls Keen, the camera accepts the new partnership and moves with the pull toward action.
treatments.movementVersusStillness: Aida’s stillness is receptive, not dominant. Bo’s motion is active but trapped: movement without progress. Keen’s motion is uncontrolled but useful once invited. The scene’s emotional change is from trapped repetition to imperfect forward motion. Stillness listens; repetition reveals; sneeze releases; invitation directs.
treatments.depthAndEnvironment: Depth carries the difference between being stuck and being summoned. The vision should feel enclosed, with Bo’s repeated packing actions unable to create distance or departure. The clearing should feel breathable by contrast, but its quiet makes Keen’s sneeze impossible to hide. Rose light lives at the margins during the vision, then lingers faintly after the sneeze so the audience feels Bo’s need is still present even while they are laughing at Keen.
treatments.rhythmAndEscalation: Begin with a tone that feels like it is asking a question. Let the packing loop answer it through repetition. Aida names the presence of need, not the diagnosis. The sneeze then changes the tempo abruptly. Aida’s honeycomb line uses the comedy to bridge back to purpose, and the final sneeze prevents the scene from becoming too solemn as it hands us into the next part of the story.
treatments.cutPhilosophy: Cuts should follow attraction: into the vision because the bowl tone pulls us there; out because the sneeze breaks the spell; onward because Aida has chosen action. Avoid cutting to “explain” Bo, Keen, or Aida. The audience should infer from behaviour: Bo repeats, Keen sneezes, Aida includes. Each cut must either change what is pulling the scene or release us from that pull.
treatments.openingImage: The bowl tone seems to draw morning light inward, as if the clearing is being gently asked where help is needed.
treatments.closingImage: The pull has changed direction: Bo’s unseen need remains ahead, Aida has chosen the way forward, and Keen follows with one last sneeze that keeps the mission lovable and imperfect.
treatments.cinematographerChallenge: Do not let the rose vision become a decorative overlay on a normal clearing scene. For this treatment to work, the vision must have gravitational authority: it temporarily owns the frame and the audience’s concern. The sneeze must then feel like a real release from that pull, not just a loud sound added over calm coverage.

treatmentSelection.selectedTreatment: The Bowl Becomes a Door, Pulled by the Vision
treatmentSelection.governingAudienceExperience: The audience is drawn into Aida’s hush until Bo’s stuckness quietly fills the world, then Keen’s uncontrollable sneeze breaks the spell and is warmly folded into the mission, so the scene exits with concern, laughter, and imperfect forward motion all ringing together.
treatmentSelection.rationale: Select Treatment 1 as the spine and Treatment 3 as the force inside it. Treatment 1 best owns the scene’s emotional truth: Aida’s private listening becomes shared action, and her choice to include Keen is the actual turn. Its circle-to-path grammar gives the scene a memorable shape without prescribing mechanical coverage. Treatment 3 strengthens that by making Bo’s vision exert real pull, so the rose image is not decorative magic but the emotional gravity of the scene. Together they keep the meaning clear: help begins in quiet attention, but it does not require a perfectly composed helper. This also gives strong contrast with the preceding honey mischief: Keen’s comic consequence crashes into Aida’s stillness, but Aida does not scold or reset him — she recruits him. The visual opportunity is specific and feasible: bowl vibration, rose vision, trapped packing loop, sneeze rupture, then movement out. The rhythm has proper breath: hush, concern, rupture, kindness, invitation, sneezy button.
treatmentSelection.rejectionChecks: Reject Treatment 2 as the governing approach, not because its pieces are unusable, but because making the clearing the primary comic straight face risks shifting the scene away from Aida’s relationship choice and Bo’s need into an environment-gag premise. It could encourage too many visible environmental reactions to the sneeze, which would drift toward action/consequence/reaction coverage rather than changed knowing. The selected combination explicitly rejects fixed character lanes, keeping all characters visible, safe elder-at-bowl staging, routine cutaways to the sneezer, repeated close-up punctuation, mechanical shot counts, generic prettiness, and merely illustrating the script. The camera must be pulled by tone, vision, rupture, and invitation — not parked to observe behaviour from safety.
